stem: Compliance records are accessed roughly once a year, must be retrievable within 12 hours when needed, must remain in place at least 180 days, and the team wants the lowest possible storage cost.
rationale: Glacier Deep Archive fits annual-or-rarer access, restores within 12 hours on its Standard retrieval tier, matches the 180-day minimum storage duration, and is the cheapest of the archival classes for data accessed this rarely. Glacier Flexible Retrieval can also meet the retrieval-time and duration requirements, but it costs more than Deep Archive for data accessed only about once a year, so it fails the lowest-cost requirement. Standard-IA is priced for infrequent but still regular access, with a 30-day minimum duration and a higher per-GB rate than the archival classes, making it more expensive for this pattern. Intelligent-Tiering is built for access patterns that are unknown or changing, and it adds a monitoring fee this known, once-a-year pattern does not need to pay.
